title: Performance Assessment & Showcase
subtitle: Four strands, one showing. You are marked on preparation as much as on talent.
objectives: Explain what a performance assessment measures
Choose a showcase piece for each of the four strands
Self-mark against a rubric before the day
Rehearse in the conditions you will perform in
Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

cards.title: This week you show it, you do not write it
cards.text: Your teacher sets the exact task. What follows is the shape almost every performance assessment takes.

cards.title: Ten weeks, one tap each
cards.text: There is still a written half. This is your revision sheet for it.

cards.title: Music, Art, PE, Health
cards.text: A showcase usually asks for something from each. Knowing that in advance is most of the preparation.
points: **Music:** perform, or describe using the elements.
**Art:** a finished piece plus your choices.
**PE:** a skill demonstrated properly.
**Health:** a habit, explained and evidenced.

question.text: What does a performance assessment measure that a written test does not?
options: Whether you can actually do the thing
question.explain: Knowing the five components of fitness and demonstrating one are different skills. This week tests the second.

cards.title: Four things get marked, almost always
cards.text: Find out the real rubric from your teacher. If you cannot, prepare against these four and you will be close.
points: **Preparation:** did you bring what you needed?
**Technique:** is it done correctly?
**Expression:** are choices visible in it?
**Presentation:** can it be seen and heard?

cards.title: Judges score what they can see
cards.text: A clean landed shot scores. A brilliant idea that never lands does not. Performance assessment works the same way.
points: **Do the visible version** of the skill.
**Slow and correct** beats fast and messy.
**Finish the movement.** Do not trail off.
**Unfinished reads as unprepared.**

question.text: Performing a skill slowly but correctly usually scores better than rushing it.
question.explain: Technique is what is being marked. Speed without control shows less, not more.

cards.title: Good place to pause
cards.text: Part 2 is rehearsal and nerves. Then a review quiz on the whole term.

cards.title: Practise in the conditions you will perform in
cards.text: Practising a song sitting down and performing it standing up are two different tasks. Your body notices.

cards.title: Run it whole, not in pieces
cards.text: Practising the hard bit over and over is useful early. Close to the day, run the whole thing without stopping.
points: **Full run-throughs**, mistakes included.
**Do not restart** when something goes wrong.
**Recovering is the skill** being tested.
**Three full runs** beat thirty partial ones.

cards.title: No save points in a performance
cards.text: You cannot reload from the last checkpoint. Practising only in sections trains you to stop when something goes wrong.
points: **A run is one attempt**, start to finish.
**Practise the recovery**, not just the part.
**Everybody slips.**
**Carrying on is what gets marked.**

cards.title: Nervous and ready are the same feeling
cards.text: A faster heart and shallow breathing are your body preparing. The same signals arrive before something you want.
points: **Name it:** this is my body getting ready.
**Breathe out longer than you breathe in.**
**Look at one friendly face**, not the room.
**Start slightly slower** than you want to.

question.text: What is the best way to rehearse in the last few days?
options: Full run-throughs without stopping for mistakes
Reading through it in your head
question.explain: Stopping at every slip trains you to stop. On the day you have to carry on.

cards.title: Warm up before you are marked
cards.text: Cold muscles move worse and cold voices crack. Five minutes of movement changes what your body can do.
points: **Move before a PE demonstration.**
**Warm the voice** before singing.
**Sleep the night before** still applies.
**None of this is superstition.**

question.text: Feeling nervous before performing means you are not ready.
question.explain: The signals are your body preparing. They arrive before things you want as well as things you fear.

cards.title: The four that matter
points: **Preparation, technique, expression, presentation.**
**Slow and correct** beats fast and messy.
**Run it whole.** Practise the recovery.
**Nervous and ready** feel the same.

quiz.text: What is the difference between dynamics and tempo?
options: Dynamics is loud and soft; tempo is the speed
Dynamics is the speed; tempo is loud and soft
quiz.explain: Week 1. Both are elements of music, and the exam swaps them regularly.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: What is self space?
options: Everything within reach from where you stand, and it travels with you
A fixed spot marked on the floor
quiz.explain: Week 1. General space is the whole area you can travel through.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: What decides a music genre?
options: Shared rhythm, instruments, place and time
quiz.explain: Week 2. Most genres grew in a place first and were labelled afterwards.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: OPM is a single music genre.
quiz.explain: Week 3. It is a statement about who made the music. OPM includes rock, rap, ballads and folk.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: Which instrument ensemble came to the Philippines through Spanish influence?
quiz.explain: Week 3. The kulintang is indigenous; the rondalla arrived with Spanish contact.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: What is the difference between shape and form?
options: Shape is two-dimensional; form is three-dimensional
Shape is coloured; form is not
Form is flat; shape is solid
quiz.explain: Week 4. A square against a cube. Both are elements of art.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: Which of these is a principle of design rather than an element of art?
quiz.explain: Week 4. Elements are what is in the picture. Principles are how they are arranged.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: Who painted the Spoliarium?
quiz.explain: Week 5. Amorsolo painted sunlit rural scenes. Luna's Spoliarium shows a Roman arena.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: Victorio Edades was admired immediately for his modern work.
quiz.explain: Week 5. His 1928 exhibition was widely disliked. The title came much later.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: Which set is the primary colours in paint?
quiz.explain: Week 6. Red, green and blue is light on a screen, not pigment.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: What do the eight rays on the Philippine flag stand for?
options: The first eight provinces to revolt
quiz.explain: Week 6. The three stars are Luzon, the Visayas and Mindanao.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: Volleyball belongs to which category of game?
quiz.explain: Week 7. A barrier separates the two sides, which changes every tactic.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: What is the national martial art and sport of the Philippines?
quiz.explain: Week 7. Basketball is far more popular, but arnis holds the official status.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: Which is a manipulative movement skill?
quiz.explain: Week 7. Manipulative skills involve handling an object.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: Thirst is an early warning that you need water.
quiz.explain: Week 8. Reaction time and endurance drop before thirst arrives.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: Which are 'grow' foods?
quiz.explain: Week 8. Go foods give energy and glow foods protect.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: Which is a health-related component of fitness?
quiz.explain: Week 9. The other three are skill-related. The exam tests exactly this boundary.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: What does FITT stand for?
quiz.explain: Week 9. Four dials on the same machine, and you change one at a time.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: The body adapts and gets stronger during the training session itself.
quiz.explain: Week 9. The session is the stress. The adaptation is built afterwards, during rest.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: What causes body odour?
options: Bacteria feeding on sweat from apocrine glands
Sweat, which has a strong smell of its own
quiz.explain: Week 10. Fresh sweat is nearly odourless. Apocrine glands switch on at puberty.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: Why does acne become common at puberty?
options: Hormones increase the skin's oil production
quiz.explain: Week 10. Scrubbing harder irritates the skin and makes it worse.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten MAPEH topics of the term

quiz.text: What gets marked in a performance assessment?
quiz.explain: Preparation is a mark you can secure entirely in advance.
quiz.objective: Self-mark against a rubric before the day

quiz.text: What is the best way to rehearse close to the day?
options: Watching a recording of someone else
quiz.explain: Stopping at every mistake trains you to stop. Recovery is what is being marked.
quiz.objective: Rehearse in the conditions you will perform in

quiz.text: Warming up before a physical demonstration changes what your body can do.
quiz.explain: Cold muscles move worse and cold voices crack. Five minutes genuinely changes the result.
quiz.objective: Rehearse in the conditions you will perform in

teacher.summary: Week 11 in MAPEH is a performance assessment rather than a written exam, and the deck is honest that the exact task comes from his teacher — it gives the shape almost every such assessment takes rather than inventing a brief. The most useful content here is the rubric, because preparation is the one criterion a student can secure completely in advance, and the rehearsal card, which argues for full run-throughs on the grounds that stopping at every slip trains you to stop. The nerves card reframes the physical signals accurately: the same arousal arrives before something wanted as before something feared. The 24-question review covers all ten weeks plus the showcase material.
discussion: Ask him to find out the real rubric from his teacher, then compare it with the four here.
Ask which of the four criteria he can secure completely before the day.
Ask what happens in a run-through when he makes a mistake, and whether he stops.
Ask him to name the four MAPEH strands and what he would show for each.
teacher.extension: Have him do three full run-throughs and note only what he did after each mistake. The recovery is the thing worth practising.
misconceptions: 'Performance assessment measures natural talent.' Preparation and technique carry most of the marks.
'Faster looks better.' Slow and correct shows technique. Rushing hides it.
'Practise the hard part until it is perfect.' Useful early, but close to the day the whole run matters more.
'Nerves mean you are not ready.' The signals are your body preparing, and they come with wanting it too.
